newsitem.title: UK: BP's Amethyst gas field down for 10-14 days.
newsitem.headline: BP's Amethyst gas field down for 10-14 days.

text.p: The Amethyst natural gas field in the southern gas basin off eastern England will be shut for about 10-14 days after an anchor from a tanker ruptured the methanol line and main power line to the platforms, operator British Petroleum Co Plc said.
Amethyst, which produces about 148 million cubic feet per day (MMcfd), has been shut since Friday when the incident occurred, said a BP spokesman.
The spokesman said BP shut off production to allow further inspection by divers of the main 30-inch export pipeline but that initial inspections showed that the pipeline had not been affected.
"We want to carry out further inspections to be extra sure that everything is OK. However, initial inspections show that the main pipeline has not been damaged," the BP spokesman said.
He said it would be "days, not weeks" before production was restarted.
"We anticipate a shutdown of 10-14 days at the most," he added.
The gas is landed at British Gas Plc's Easington terminal.
